## Program

<a id="program"></a>

### Program

A Teletronix program: its settings, screens and dialogs

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | string |  | Path or URL of teletronix.schema.json, for checking and autocomplete in editors |
| `config` | [Config](#config) | **required** | Settings for the whole program |
| `screens` | map of id → [Screen](#screen) | **required** | The screens, by id. Links, commands and `next` refer to them by id. |
| `dialogs` | map of id → [Alert](#alert) \| [Confirm](#confirm) |  | The dialogs, by id. Actions open them by id. |

<a id="config"></a>

### Config

Settings for the whole program. `reveal`, `transition`, `effects` and `autoscroll` apply to every screen unless it sets its own.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | The program's name, shown as the page title |
| `author` | string |  | Who made it |
| `description` | string |  | What it is |
| `start` | id | the first one | The first screen |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | `"teletype"` | How text appears on every screen, unless a screen or element says otherwise |
| `transition` | [Transition](#transition) | `"none"` | How screens leave, unless the next screen says otherwise |
| `defaults` | [Defaults](#defaults) |  | Default options for each kind of reveal |
| `theme` | [Theme](#theme) | `"default"` | The color scheme: "default" (pale blue on black), "amber", "green" or "white", or your own colors |
| `font` | `"ast-premiumexec"` \| `"ibm-vga"` \| `"ibm-ega"` \| `"ibm-cga"` \| `"ibm-cga-thin"` \| `"ibm-mda"` \| `"toshiba-satellite"` \| `"departure-mono"` | `"ast-premiumexec"` | The typeface, from a set of period PC fonts |
| `effects` | [Effects](#effects) |  | Visual effects: true, false, or an object of options |
| `sound` | [Sound](#sound) |  | Generated retro sound effects: true, false, or an object of options. On by default; players can mute them with the sound toggle. |
| `blockContextMenu` | boolean | `true` | Block the browser's right-click menu, so the program feels like a terminal rather than a web page. Text fields keep theirs |
| `autoscroll` | boolean | `true` | Scroll to keep new content in view as it appears, unless the reader has scrolled up |

<a id="defaults"></a>

### Defaults

Default options for each kind of reveal

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `teletype` | [Teletype options](#teletype-options) |  | Default teletype options |
| `glitch` | [Glitch options](#glitch-options) |  | Default glitch options, for reveals and transitions |

<a id="teletype-options"></a>

### Teletype options

Default options for teletype reveals

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | number, > 0 | `10` | Milliseconds per character |

<a id="glitch-options"></a>

### Glitch options

Default options for glitch reveals and transitions

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | number, > 0 | `1000` | Milliseconds a glitch takes |

<a id="screen"></a>

### Screen

A screen of content. Its elements are revealed one after another.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) |  | Default reveal for this screen's elements |
| `transition` | [Transition](#transition) |  | How the previous screen leaves when this one is shown |
| `effects` | [Effects](#effects) |  | Effects for this screen, layered over the config's |
| `autoscroll` | boolean | the config's | Keep new content in view as it appears |
| `next` | [Next rule](#next-rule) \| [Next rule](#next-rule)[] |  | Moves on without a link: after a delay, at a key press, or both. One rule, or a list where the first rule to trigger wins. With empty content and full-opacity static, this makes a burst of noise between screens. |
| `content` | (string \| [Text](#text) \| [Link](#link) \| [Toggle](#toggle) \| [Prompt](#prompt) \| [Bitmap](#bitmap) \| [Progress](#progress) \| [Slider](#slider))[] | **required** | The elements, revealed in order. Can be empty. |

<a id="next-rule"></a>

### Next rule

A way to move on from a screen without a link: after a delay, at a key press, or both

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | number, ≥ 0 |  | Milliseconds to wait after the screen has finished revealing |
| `key` | string \| string[] |  | A key that moves on: "any", a key name like "Enter", "Space", "Escape", "ArrowRight" or "y", or an array of them. Taps and clicks count too, unless keys in different rules lead to different places. |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | Where to go |

## Elements

<a id="text"></a>

### Text (`"type": "text", or a bare string`)

A block of text. A bare string is shorthand for this.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | **required** | The text to display. May contain line breaks. |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="link"></a>

### Link (`"type": "link"`)

Clickable text that navigates to a screen or opens a dialog

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | **required** | The link's text |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | What happens when the link is clicked |
| `secondaryAction` | [Action](#action) | the same as action | What happens on a secondary click: shift-click, right-click, Shift+Enter, or a long press |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="toggle"></a>

### Toggle (`"type": "toggle"`)

Text that cycles through states when clicked. It remembers its state when you come back.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `states` | string[] | **required** | The texts to cycle through, one per click |
| `initial` | whole number, ≥ 0 | `0` | Index of the state shown first |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="prompt"></a>

### Prompt (`"type": "prompt"`)

A command line. Typed commands navigate or open dialogs.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prompt` | string | `"> "` | Text shown before the input |
| `commands` | [Prompt command](#prompt-command)[] | **required** | The commands it understands |
| `unknown` | string | `"Unknown command."` | Shown when the input matches no command |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="prompt-command"></a>

### Prompt command

A command the prompt understands

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string \| string[] | **required** | What to type (case-insensitive). Use an array for aliases. |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | What happens when the command is entered |

<a id="bitmap"></a>

### Bitmap (`"type": "bitmap"`)

An image, revealed in steps from low to high resolution, optionally blended with the screen's colors

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | string | **required** | Image URL, or a path relative to the page |
| `alt` | string | **required** | A description of the image, for screen readers |
| `blend` | [Blend](#blend) |  | Blends the image with one of the theme's colors: a mode such as "luminosity", "hard-light" or "difference", or { "mode", "with": "text" } to blend with the text color instead of the background |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="blend"></a>

### Blend

Blends the image with one of the theme's colors: a mode such as "luminosity", "hard-light" or "difference", or { "mode", "with": "text" } to blend with the text color instead of the background

One of:

- `"luminosity"` | `"lighten"` | `"darken"` | `"multiply"` | `"screen"` | `"overlay"` | `"color-dodge"` | `"color-burn"` | `"hard-light"` | `"soft-light"` | `"difference"` | `"exclusion"` | `"hue"` | `"saturation"` | `"color"`: How the colors combine
- [Blend with a color](#blend-with-a-color)

<a id="blend-with-a-color"></a>

### Blend with a color

A blend mode, and the theme color to blend with

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"luminosity"` \| `"lighten"` \| `"darken"` \| `"multiply"` \| `"screen"` \| `"overlay"` \| `"color-dodge"` \| `"color-burn"` \| `"hard-light"` \| `"soft-light"` \| `"difference"` \| `"exclusion"` \| `"hue"` \| `"saturation"` \| `"color"` | **required** | How the colors combine |
| `with` | `"background"` \| `"text"` | `"background"` | The theme color to blend with |

<a id="progress"></a>

### Progress (`"type": "progress"`)

A text progress bar that runs from one percentage to another over a set time, then carries on, or runs an action

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string |  | Text before the bar |
| `from` | number, 0–100 | `0` | Starting percentage |
| `to` | number, 0–100 | `100` | Final percentage (default: 100). Lower than `from` runs backwards. |
| `duration` | number, > 0 | `2000` | Milliseconds to go from `from` to `to` |
| `percent` | boolean | `true` | Show the current value |
| `width` | whole number, ≥ 1 | the rest of the line | Bar width in characters |
| `fill` | character | `"█"` | Filled cells |
| `empty` | character | `"░"` | Empty cells |
| `onComplete` | [Progress outcome](#progress-outcome) |  | What happens when the bar reaches `to`: an action, or { after, action } to pause first. Without one, the screen carries on. |
| `interrupt` | [Progress interrupt](#progress-interrupt) |  | Makes the bar stop short, at a set point (`at`) or a key press (`key`) |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="progress-outcome"></a>

### Progress outcome

What happens when a progress bar finishes: an action, now or after a pause

One of:

- [Screen action](#screen-action)
- [Dialog action](#dialog-action)
- [Delayed action](#delayed-action)

<a id="delayed-action"></a>

### Delayed action

An action that runs after a pause

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | number, ≥ 0 |  | Milliseconds to wait first |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | What happens |

<a id="progress-interrupt"></a>

### Progress interrupt

Makes a progress bar stop short: at a set point (a transfer that fails) and/or when the player presses a key

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | number, 0–100 |  | Stop here instead of reaching `to`: a transfer that fails |
| `key` | string \| string[] |  | A key that aborts the bar while it runs: "any", a key name, or an array |
| `text` | string | `"INTERRUPTED"` | Shown in place of the percentage |
| `action` | [Action](#action) |  | What happens when interrupted, instead of onComplete |
| `after` | number, ≥ 0 |  | Milliseconds to wait before the action |

<a id="slider"></a>

### Slider (`"type": "slider"`)

A bar the player sets by dragging, or with the arrow keys. It remembers its value, and can run actions when the value enters a range.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string |  | Text before the bar |
| `min` | number | `0` | The lowest value |
| `max` | number | `100` | The highest value |
| `step` | number, > 0 | `1` | The smallest change, e.g. 5, or 0.1 |
| `value` | number | min | Where it starts |
| `unit` | string | `""` | Shown after the value, e.g. "%" or " MHz" |
| `showValue` | boolean | `true` | Show the value after the bar |
| `width` | whole number, ≥ 1 | the rest of the line | Bar width in characters |
| `fill` | character | `"█"` | Filled cells |
| `empty` | character | `"░"` | Empty cells |
| `on` | [Slider rule](#slider-rule)[] |  | Actions for ranges of values. The first rule the value moves into fires. |
| `onEnter` | [Action](#action) |  | What happens when the player presses <enter> on the slider |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes, e.g. "alert" |
| `reveal` | [Reveal](#reveal) | the screen's reveal | How this element's text appears |

<a id="slider-rule"></a>

### Slider rule

An action for a range of values. It fires each time the value moves into the range; set more than one condition and the value must meet them all.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atLeast` | number |  | Fires when the value rises to this or above |
| `atMost` | number |  | Fires when the value falls to this or below |
| `equals` | number |  | Fires when the value lands on exactly this |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | What happens |

## Dialogs

<a id="alert"></a>

### Alert (`"type": "alert"`)

A message. Closes with <enter>, <esc>, or a click.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string \| string[] | **required** | The dialog's text: a string, or an array of paragraphs |
| `dismiss` | string | `"OK"` | The button that closes it |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes |

<a id="confirm"></a>

### Confirm (`"type": "confirm"`)

A yes/no question. Each answer can trigger an action.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string \| string[] | **required** | The dialog's text: a string, or an array of paragraphs |
| `confirm` | [Confirm button](#confirm-button) | **required** | The "yes" button, chosen with <enter> |
| `cancel` | [Cancel button](#cancel-button) |  | The "no" button, chosen with <esc> or a click outside the dialog |
| `className` | string |  | Space-separated CSS classes |

<a id="confirm-button"></a>

### Confirm button

The "yes" button, chosen with <enter>

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | `"YES"` | The label |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | **required** | What happens when it's chosen |

<a id="cancel-button"></a>

### Cancel button

The "no" button, chosen with <esc> or a click outside the dialog

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | `"NO"` | The label |
| `action` | [Action](#action) | nothing; the dialog closes | What happens when it's chosen |

## Appearance

<a id="theme"></a>

### Theme

The color scheme: "default" (pale blue on black), "amber", "green" or "white", or your own colors (default: "default")

One of:

- `"default"` | `"amber"` | `"green"` | `"white"`
- [Custom theme](#custom-theme)

<a id="custom-theme"></a>

### Custom theme

Your own colors

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fg` | id | **required** | Text color |
| `bg` | id | **required** | Background color |
| `alert` | id | `"#ff3c00"` | Color of text with the "alert" class |

<a id="sound"></a>

### Sound

Generated retro sound effects: true, false, or an object of options. On by default; players can mute them with the sound toggle.

One of:

- boolean
- [Sound options](#sound-options)

<a id="sound-options"></a>

### Sound options

Sound options: the volume, and each kind of sound on or off

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume` | number, 0–1 | `0.3` | Overall volume, from 0 to 1 |
| `typing` | boolean | `true` | Key clicks as text types in |
| `glitch` | boolean | `true` | Digital crackle during glitch reveals and transitions |
| `static` | boolean | `true` | Hiss under static, and the static transition |
| `interface` | boolean | `true` | Beeps for links, toggles, sliders, prompts and dialogs |
| `hum` | boolean | `false` | A CRT's mains hum and high-pitched whine, all the time |

## Effects

<a id="effects"></a>

### Effects

Visual effects: true, false, or an object of options

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scanlines` | boolean \| [Scanlines](#scanlines) |  | CRT scanlines (on by default) |
| `static` | boolean \| [Static](#static) |  | Analog TV noise (off by default) |
| `bloom` | boolean \| [Bloom](#bloom) |  | Glow around bright things (off by default) |
| `vignette` | boolean \| [Vignette](#vignette) |  | Darkened corners (off by default) |
| `flicker` | boolean \| [Flicker](#flicker) |  | An unsteady, dimming picture (off by default) |
| `fringe` | boolean \| [Fringe](#fringe) |  | Red and cyan color fringes on text (off by default) |

<a id="scanlines"></a>

### Scanlines (`"scanlines"`)

CRT scanlines, with an optional rolling band. On by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | number, 0–1 | `0.5` | Strength of the lines, from 0 to 1 |
| `moving` | boolean | `true` | Roll a bright line down the screen |

<a id="static"></a>

### Static (`"static"`)

Analog TV noise over the screen. Off by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | number, 0–1 | `0.15` | Strength of the noise, from 0 to 1 |
| `fps` | number, 1–60 | `24` | Noise frames per second |
| `scale` | whole number, 1–16 | `3` | Size of a noise pixel, in screen pixels |

<a id="bloom"></a>

### Bloom (`"bloom"`)

Bright text and images glow into the dark around them. Off by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | number, 0–1 | `0.5` | From 0 to 1 |
| `radius` | number, 1–32 | `8` | How far the glow spreads, in pixels |

<a id="vignette"></a>

### Vignette (`"vignette"`)

Darkened corners, like the edge of a curved tube. Off by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | number, 0–1 | `0.6` | From 0 to 1 |

<a id="flicker"></a>

### Flicker (`"flicker"`)

An unsteady picture that dims by small, irregular amounts. Off by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | number, 0–1 | `0.5` | From 0 to 1 |

<a id="fringe"></a>

### Fringe (`"fringe"`)

Red and cyan fringes on text, like misaligned color guns. Off by default.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | number, 0–1 | `0.6` | From 0 to 1 |
| `offset` | number, 0.5–8 | `1` | How far the colors split, in pixels |

## Shared types

<a id="action"></a>

### Action

What an interactive element does: go to a screen, or open a dialog

One of:

- [Screen action](#screen-action)
- [Dialog action](#dialog-action)

<a id="screen-action"></a>

### Screen action

Navigate to a screen

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `screen` | id | **required** | A screen or dialog id (letters, digits, '_' and '-') |

<a id="dialog-action"></a>

### Dialog action

Open a dialog

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dialog` | id | **required** | A screen or dialog id (letters, digits, '_' and '-') |

<a id="reveal"></a>

### Reveal

How text appears: "teletype" (character by character), "glitch" (resolves out of random glyphs) or "instant" (all at once). Use an object to override options, e.g. { "type": "teletype", "speed": 20 }. When a screen or the config sets "glitch", consecutive elements that don't set their own reveal glitch in together as one block.

One of:

- `"teletype"` | `"glitch"` | `"instant"`
- [Teletype reveal](#teletype-reveal)
- [Glitch reveal](#glitch-reveal)
- [Instant reveal](#instant-reveal)

<a id="teletype-reveal"></a>

### Teletype reveal (`"type": "teletype"`)

Types the text one character at a time

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | number, > 0 | `10` | Milliseconds per character |

<a id="glitch-reveal"></a>

### Glitch reveal (`"type": "glitch"`)

Resolves the text out of random glyphs, left to right

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | number, > 0 | config.defaults.glitch | Milliseconds for the text to resolve |

<a id="instant-reveal"></a>

### Instant reveal (`"type": "instant"`)

Shows the text all at once

No options.

<a id="transition"></a>

### Transition

How the previous screen leaves: "none" (it disappears at once), "glitch" (it erases itself over this screen while this screen reveals), "fade" (it fades out like phosphor afterglow) or "static" (a brief burst of full-screen noise, like changing channels, before this screen reveals)

One of:

- `"none"` | `"glitch"` | `"fade"` | `"static"`
- [No transition](#no-transition)
- [Glitch transition](#glitch-transition)
- [Fade transition](#fade-transition)
- [Static transition](#static-transition)

<a id="no-transition"></a>

### No transition (`"type": "none"`)

The old screen disappears at once

No options.

<a id="glitch-transition"></a>

### Glitch transition (`"type": "glitch"`)

The old screen erases itself over the new one as it appears

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | number, > 0 | config.defaults.glitch | Milliseconds for the old screen to erase |

<a id="fade-transition"></a>

### Fade transition (`"type": "fade"`)

The old screen fades out behind the new one, like phosphor afterglow

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | number, > 0 | `600` | Milliseconds to fade out |

<a id="static-transition"></a>

### Static transition (`"type": "static"`)

A brief burst of full-screen noise, like changing channels, before the new screen

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | number, > 0 | `120` | Milliseconds of static |
